subject: Life Skills
title: Consistency Over Grand Gestures
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Consistency Over Grand Gestures.

hook.text: He sent flowers after every argument. She wanted something simpler: showing up on time and keeping his word.

buildup.text: Trust is built in small, repeated moments — not big, dramatic ones. It is a drip, not a flood.

discovery.text: Following through on tiny promises — calling when you said you would, arriving when expected — signals deep reliability.

twist.text: One betrayal erases dozens of good moments. Trust falls faster than it builds because violations linger deeply.

climax.text: Make fewer promises but keep all of them. Under-promise and over-deliver is the oldest trust hack and it still works.

punchline.text: Small promises kept daily beat grand gestures yearly.

quiz.question: Why do small promises matter more than grand gestures for trust?
options: Trust is built through repeated, consistent follow-through over time
People do not notice grand gestures
